ruling.recommended_action: Close the case: no route deviation and no overcharge on this RydeTAXI trip; send the rider a plain-language explanation that heavy rain increased metered time (not distance), so the fare exceeded the pre-trip estimate.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen first: the complaint ("the fare was higher than I expected … the driver must have taken a longer route"), the driver's statement [F7] and the (empty) chat record [F6] contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and the dispute type is route_deviation, not safety — safety_concern = none.

Merits. RD-1 requires identifying at least one "off-route segment". The GPS record shows actual distance 8.5 km against an optimal-route distance of 8.5 km, +0.0 km (-0%) [F1], and the billed distance likewise does not exceed the optimal route [F3]. There is therefore no off-route segment and no extra mileage: no RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5 exemption analysis is needed and the RD-6 precondition (a case established against the driver, i.e. RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) is not met — indeed the driver profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F13].

The higher-than-expected total is fully explained by time, not distance. This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the fare follows the taxi meter: distance $11.99 (8.50 km) + time $5.72 (22.0 min) + base $3.90 + platform $1.47 = $23.08 [F5], with no surge [F4], no waiting fee, and no undisclosed surcharge. Duration was 22.0 min against the 16.3-min estimate (+5.7 min) [F2], and the cause is documented in the record: heavy rain, 18.5 mm thundery showers [F11], with PIE and Airport Boulevard both in speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) across 17:09–17:47 [F8][F9]; no incidents were recorded [F10]. Because the driver's meter charges for waiting/slow-moving time (RD-3(c) / RD-2 note for metered taxis), a slow rainy trip legitimately costs more than the pre-trip estimate even on the identical 8.5 km route. Nothing was added beyond the metered fare and the published platform fee, so FARE-1 is not engaged either. No item to refund; amount = null.

Evidence status is sufficient: GPS totals, fare breakdown and traffic/weather records settle every element I need; there is no missing or gap-flagged record (no detour facts to evaluate, chat absence is itself the recorded state, and RD-5 is not in issue because no route change occurred). No segment findings. Rider's claim rejected as disproved by [F1][F3][F5].

rejected_claims.reason: Disproved by system records: actual distance equals the optimal route (+0.0 km) and the billed distance does not exceed it, so there is no off-route segment under RD-1; the higher fare is explained by slow rain-affected metered time, not by extra mileage.
